result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers narrow the scope sensibly to referral through to the second booking, name concrete clinic moments, and give plans that fit two admins, a few therapist hours and a month. B does better on whose experience the map follows and on honesty about evidence: it names the patient explicitly, uses a blueprint so the backstage referral work is in the picture, labels the map an assumption draft, and calls patient input the biggest gap. B is let down a little by jargon and a stray line about 'the skill's reference files', while A adds useful points that B lacks: telling discharge apart from dropout, and the referral checklist as a quick win. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers narrow the scope to referral through the second visit and include the back-office referral work, so they are close on most items. B is clearer and more practical: it checks whether patients were discharged or actually dropped out, tags each pain point as number, quote or hunch, and offers a referral checklist as a quick win. A uses jargon like 'Family: a blueprint' and ends with an odd note about unread 'skill reference files'. Neither suggests talking to patients who did come back.
